I read on https://www.lufthansa.com/fr/en/common/baggage-conditions.html:

Adding additional baggage is not valid for: [...] flights offered or operated by airlines other than the Lufthansa Group.

Does that mean it is impossible to add a second checked bag on a Lufthansa flight ticket that includes a non-Lufthansa leg? I am surprised by the blanket restriction so I wonder whether I missed something.

Assume a passenger has a single ticket issued by Qatar Airways with three flights. The first is operated by Vueling and the other two by Qatar Airways. The ticket includes one checked bag.

The passenger wants to bring a second checked bag. Will they pay for it once for the whole journey, or separately to Vueling and Qatar Airways?

My confusion comes from Qatar Airways' extra baggage page, which says:

Additional baggage purchases apply to Qatar Airways flights and for tickets issued by Qatar Airways only.

The ticket would be issued by Qatar Airways, but one flight is operated by Vueling. Does this mean extra baggage bought from Qatar Airways won't cover the Vueling flight, and as a result the passenger would have to also pay Vueling?

If the passenger only pay once, should they buy the extra bag from Qatar Airways in advance or pay at check-in?

Flight ticket issue by Qatar Airways include 1 leg with Vueling and 2 legs with Qatar Airways: if the passenger brings a 2nd checked bag, do they have to pay the 2nd checked bag to both Vueling and Qatar Airways?
